answer: Continuous presence audit. Each identity must answer random micro-tasks at unpredictable intervals tied to a drifting clock seeded from a wharf sensor feed, so sustained attention is the scarce input. Misses accumulate on a public island ledger until the identity's score falls below a threshold, at which point its votes and payments are frozen. An attacker running N identities pays N times the attention cost, and any delta between peak and trough activity reveals farming, forcing continuous human staffing per identity rather than one-time registration.
